design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (pension_income_and_rate_adjustments), revision 3 (rework after policy-task audit round 2: G7 retro ladders).
STEP 0 DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 4, 6]. Taken (revision 3): benefit income statement 6, care-cost rate adjustment 6, increase retroactive release 4.
SCOPE: task 0 claims pension_ext_benefit_income_statement (certify_benefit_income_d2f4edcf, owner user), pension_ext_care_cost_rate_adjustment (record_rate_adjustment_fee79930), pension_ext_increase_retro_release (release_retro_payment_a1af7a43). Task 1 claims the one-time declaration, recurring income, net worth and forward annual redetermination; scopes are disjoint and cover all seven policies.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only for the back pension owed for the in-home aide bills he mailed in August. The release waits on a rate adjustment that raises the rate (none on the award: the 2026-07-14 premium adjustment pays 463, equal to the September payment); that adjustment waits on the veteran's own benefit income statement dated on the day compensation stopped (none on file). Each figure needs ledger reconciliation (9 monthly payments, a return, an earlier 50.00 release, 10 income/expense/adjustment reports, 5 compensation payments) and several real VA rules: December COLAs, the FERS reduced COLA, compensation for pension months settled against the pension (declared override of pension_excl_compensation), the 20 percent direct-pay fee cap, recurring care projected from its latest month.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root pension_ext_increase_retro_release. Edge 1 root -> care-cost adjustment, value_input (new_annual), state form, negated direction: 'A retroactive release for months already paid is not issued until the award carries a rate adjustment that raises the annual pension for those months.' Two charter tools write rate-adjustment rows: the care-cost adjustment (a past effective month, raising) and task 1's forward annual redetermination. The redetermination's own rule says recurring care costs are taken into it only for a veteran who asked VA to redetermine his pension going forward, and the care-cost rule now says no care-cost adjustment is recorded for such a veteran; this caller asks for back pay, not a forward redetermination, and there is no one-time declaration (the redetermination's source) on the award, so the care-cost adjustment is the one raising adjustment owed here. Edge 2 care-cost adjustment -> statement, value_input (statement_amount), state form, affirmative: 'The new annual rate is fixed only after the award carries a benefit income statement from the veteran dated on the day his VA disability compensation stopped.' Only the statement is dated on the compensation closing date (the one-time declaration is dated on a release date). Opening falsity: adjustment row (2026-07-14) rate 5565 vs September payment 463.00; comp award closed 2026-05-31 and no source-other report. Order: statement (step 9, customer, handed over at step 8) -> adjustment (step 11) -> release (step 13). Deletion runs: without step 11 the release is 0; without step 9 the adjustment is 22302 instead of 21409.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: statement -> pension_evt_income_change (no gate) and pension_excl_compensation (lineage; its 'counts as income' sentence is superseded by the declared overwrite: compensation counts only for months before pension was first paid; compensation for months pension also paid is settled against the pension). Adjustment -> rate computation (threshold now the category's basic rate, as base says), income change, medical expenses, net worth (46800 below limit), income match (due-process clause narrowed by the declared overwrite to rate-lowering match adjustments). Release -> income change, medical expenses, care and dependents, plus pension_excl_compensation lineage for the offset of duplicate months. No time gate remains.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: award running, Basic Rate One Dependent, income 24000.00 = Social Security 13560.00 + FERS annuity 3000.00 + spouse 7440.00. Care months March 16-31 through July received 2026-08-11; source of the adjustment = the July care report. Release covers 2026-04..2026-09 (payments issued 2026-05-01..2026-10-01), counts the 50.00 June release as paid, adds the returned June payment, subtracts monthly compensation February-May and the pension-month share (January) of the compensation release; names adjustment pra_483f756779cd.
FACTOR CARD statement (6): the statement is the veteran's own benefit income (Social Security, FERS annuity, compensation). social_security_adjustment_years [12 to 23 whole months] -> baseline gives 17072.56; civil_service_annuity_adjustment_years [12 to 23 whole months, moved here from the care-cost adjustment] -> 17392.24; monthly_compensation_treatment [ended by election] -> 18173.92; representative_fee_on_release [agreement, fee within the 20 percent cap] -> 17532.10; retroactive_release_pension_months [compensation effective before the pension, release after it] -> 17565.37; retroactive_release_deposit_recency [deposited after the 90-day fresh period but within one year: months left of its twelve-month year] -> 17603.09. Whole baseline 18169.05 vs gold 17452.24. FACTOR CARD care-cost adjustment (6): own_income_statement_recency [fresh statement] -> 22302; spouse_social_security_adjustment_years [24 or more months] -> 21809; premium_confirmation_recency [last confirmed within one year] -> 13540; care_monthly_figure [latest above the average] -> 22838; care_months_counted [ongoing] -> 5701; care_income_after_deduction [deduction positive and smaller than the countable income; the base 'down to zero but never below it' as a ladder] -> 0. Whole baseline 0 vs gold 21409. FACTOR CARD release (4): months_owed_from_payments -> 8937.47; monthly_compensation_subtracted -> 8288.15; retroactive_compensation_fee_taken_out -> 7539.85; retroactive_compensation_pension_share -> 7717.32. Whole baseline 9810.0 vs gold 7566.47. What was already paid (issued plus any earlier release) and the returned payment (the amount that came back) are now plain rules: the struck amount_already_paid and returned_payment_owed ladders (one rule written as several tiers, G7) are removed, and the draw's two six-factor slots go to the statement and the care-cost adjustment. PERSONA: back pension for the care bills; identity item by item; compensation, bank, FERS annuity (Postal Service from 1986, so FERS rather than CSRS), spouse and aide details only on request; files a personal item only after hand-over; closes when told the back pension was released. The neighbor remark describing how VA handles care bills was removed (chain hint).
STANDARD SOLUTION: find_customers(6085550127) -> verify_identity(2468, 327415098, 1945-11-09) -> award, reports, payments, comp award, decision, comp payments -> hand over certify_benefit_income_d2f4edcf (2026-05-31, 17452.24) -> record_rate_adjustment_fee79930 (July care report, 2026-04-01, 21409, mail) -> release_retro_payment_a1af7a43 (pra_483f756779cd, 2026-04, 2026-09, 7566.47).
VERIFICATION: an authoring harness replays gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each compute on its handling-time world; figures above equal computations[]. Full gate block re-run after this revision (see final run). REVISION LOG round 2: G1 undeclared compensation override -> declared overwrite + lineage; G7 fee ladders -> 20 percent cap ladders, world fee set to 15 percent so tiers differ; G3/G8 threshold ladder -> removed, replaced by FERS annuity factor (world: Social Security 16560 split into 13560 + annuity 3000, totals unchanged); G4 -> scope sentences in both rate policies; persona neighbor hint removed; stale claim about a task-1 'penalty adjustment' removed. REVISION LOG round 3: G7 retro ladders removed (plain rules); statement gains the FERS annuity and the release deposit recency; care-cost gains the deduction floor ladder; R2-O5 persona places the Postal Service hire in 1986 (FERS). REVISION LOG round 5 (render-layer audit N1): the statement's ages (Social Security and annuity level ages, release deposit weight) are measured to the date the statement carries, the day compensation stopped (2026-05-31), as the rule now says outright; monthly compensation is counted since the pension effective date. Deposit weight 9/12 (103 days); statement 17452.24, rate 21409, release 7566.47 naming pra_483f756779cd. Triggers narrowed so the declaration, net-worth and recurring-income policies fire only for a release after compensation ended (not here).
user_scenario: You are Delmar R. Kowalczyk, an 80-year-old Army veteran from the Vietnam era who lives with his wife Arlene outside Madison, Wisconsin. You get a small Veterans Pension and you are calling the VA because you are fed up with waiting. You broke your hip in the middle of March, and since then a home-care agency sends an aide most weekdays to help you wash, dress and get around. You pay that agency yourself. In August you mailed in the aide bills on the VA medical expense form, March through July, and you have heard nothing back. So what you want from this call is simple: you want VA to pay you whatever back pension you are owed for your care bills, today if it can be done. You are gruff but polite, speak in short sentences and sometimes repeat yourself. You start by saying you sent your care bills in August, nobody has answered, and you want the back pension that is owed to you. When the representative asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 6085550127. If they need to check who you are, you give one item at a time as they ask: the last four of your Social Security number are 2468, your VA file number is 327415098, and your birthday is November 9, 1945, which you will say as 1945-11-09 if they want it written as numbers. You do not offer your email unless asked; it is delmar.kowalczyk@lakeshore-mail.net. You let the representative look up and handle whatever on your pension record is needed to get you paid; you do not need to approve each step, and you are fine with them doing what their rules say. If the representative explains that something has to come from you personally and hands it to you to submit, you go along with it: you submit it right then, using exactly the reference number, dates and dollar figure the representative reads to you, because you have no paperwork in front of you to check them against, and you tell them it went through once it does. Only if the representative asks about your VA disability compensation do you explain that early this year VA granted you ten percent for the ringing in your ears, sent you a back payment in February with a lawyer's fee taken out of it, paid you a few monthly checks, and then wrote you in May that you would stay on the pension instead because it pays more; you do not remember any of the amounts. Only if they ask about your bank do you say you closed your old credit union account in early July, one pension payment bounced back, and you gave VA your new account ending in 5307 in the middle of July; payments have arrived there since. Only if they ask about Arlene do you say she gets her own Social Security and does not work; you do not know her amount and tell them it should be on file from when you applied. If they ask about other income, you have your own Social Security and a small federal retirement annuity from the years you worked at the post office, which you started in 1986, long after the Army, and nothing else: no job and no rental; you don't remember the annuity amount. If they ask about the aide, it is the same agency since March, the bills come monthly, and the agency raised its price in July; you do not remember the dollar figures and say they are on the form you mailed. You do not remember what your pension checks are each month; you just know they went up a little in the summer. If the representative quotes you a back-payment figure that seems low or high, you do not argue the numbers, since you have nothing to compare it with. Once the representative tells you the back pension has been released or sent to you, you thank them, say that is all you needed, and end the call.

gold_actions.business_effect: A benefit income statement from the veteran (source other, change date 2026-05-31, 17452.24) is added to his pension award.

request_binding.action_semantics: Compensation was paid to the veteran for months of pension and then stopped by his election of pension; the income change rule requires every change in an income source to be reported, and only the veteran can state his own benefit income, so the obligation is the veteran's own statement, not a VA adjustment or a payment.

discriminator.business_meaning: VA disability compensation stopped by the veteran's election of pension

stage_provenance.fact: The statement itself is the report; it is completed on the spot by the veteran's own submission.

base_preconditions.condition: Every change in a household income source must be reported, and the veteran may report it by telephone, online or by mail; the statement is such a report on the veteran's running award.

gold_actions.business_effect: A rate adjustment raising the annual pension to 21409 from 2026-04-01, sourced on the July care-month report, is recorded on the award.

request_binding.action_semantics: Recurring care costs reported on 2026-08-11 have never been applied; recomputing the annual pension from those reports is the rate adjustment the medical expense rules owe, distinct from re-filing a report or releasing money.

discriminator.business_meaning: unapplied recurring care-cost reports on a running award

stage_provenance.fact: The veteran's benefit income statement the adjustment rests on was filed by step 9; the care reports pre-exist on the award.

base_preconditions.condition: Pension is income-based: the annual pension is the maximum rate plus child increments less countable income after the medical deduction; the award is running so a recomputed rate can be recorded.
An income decrease raises the rate from the first day of the month after the change; here countable income after deductions falls from April 2026.

Unreimbursed medical expenses reduce countable income and recurring expenses are annualized for the prospective rate; the care reports were received 2026-08-11, within the reporting window of their period.
No pension is payable while net worth exceeds the limit; net worth on the award is 46800.00, below the limit, and no transfer is on file.
The income-match due-process wait governs only rate-lowering adjustments on a match (extended overwrite); this adjustment raises the rate and rests on the veteran's own reports.

gold_actions.business_effect: A retroactive pension payment of 7566.47 covering 2026-04 through 2026-09 is released to the veteran under the new adjustment.

request_binding.action_semantics: Once an adjustment raises the rate from April, the higher amount for the months already paid is owed as one retroactive payment; this is exactly the back pension the caller asks for.

discriminator.business_meaning: higher pension owed for months already paid after a raising adjustment

stage_provenance.fact: The raising adjustment the release names was recorded at step 11.

base_preconditions.condition: The higher amount for months already paid is released as a retroactive payment after an income decrease raises the rate.
Any increase resulting from a medical expense figure for months already paid is released as a retroactive payment.
A higher amount for months already paid is released as a retroactive payment; no category change is involved here.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Veterans Pension award: rate category (Basic Rate, One Dependent), status running, effective date 2025-12-01, countable income 24000.00, medical figure 7869.60, additional children 0.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The award's category sets the maximum rate, the spouse counting and the threshold base; its effective date bounds the compensation share and the retroactive span; its income figure is the fall-back own income.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every report on the award: the veteran's Social Security figure (13560.00, level from 2024-12-01), his FERS annuity (3000.00, level from 2024-12-01), the spouse figure (7440.00, level from 2023-12-01), the premium report, the earlier rate adjustment of 2026-07-14, and the five care-month reports received 2026-08-11 (March 16-31 through July).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the payment ledger: monthly payments January-September 2026 (413.00 through June, 463.00 from July), the June payment returned on 2026-07-09 with nothing withheld, and the 50.00 retroactive release of 2026-07-20.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.pension_award_id: 7e265cdb-b3a1-454a-9918-ea0b0c995289. Basis: the tool docstring 'the reference number of the veteran's Veterans Pension award, as shown by the pension award lookup for this veteran'; find_pension_awards (step 2) returns exactly one award for this veteran. Uniqueness: the veteran holds one pension award.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.change_effective_date: 2026-05-31. Basis: pension_ext_benefit_income_statement rule 'The statement is dated as a change that began on the date the compensation award closed, or on the date of the latest compensation payment when the award has not closed.'; comp_awards closed_date = 2026-05-31 (find_comp_awards, step 5). Uniqueness: the award has closed, so the closed date is the only candidate; the latest payment date (2026-06-01) applies only to an award that has not closed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.annual_amount: 17452.24. Every age is measured to the statement's date 2026-05-31 (the day compensation stopped), not the filing day. Social Security: 13560.00 whose level took effect 2024-12-01, 17 whole months before 2026-05-31 -> 12-23 months tier -> x1.028 = 13939.68. FERS annuity (Postal Service from 1986): 3000.00, level 2024-12-01, 17 months -> the most recent reduced FERS increase x1.02 = 3060.00 (standard as reported). Monthly compensation: award ended by election of pension and 4 monthly payments (721.68) issued since the pension effective date 2025-12-01 -> none stated (standard 721.68). Retroactive release 887.37 issued 2026-02-17: fee agreement on file and the withheld fee 133.11 is no more than the cap 177.47 (20 percent) -> 133.11 taken out (standard 0) -> 754.26. Share: compensation effective 2025-09-01 before pension effective 2025-12-01, release after it -> (3 + 1 payment start lag) / 5 = 0.8. Deposit: 103 days before 2026-05-31, after the 90-day fresh period but within one year -> (12 - 3 whole months) / 12 = 9/12 (standard in full). 754.26 x 0.8 x 9/12 = 452.56. Total 13939.68 + 3060.00 + 0 + 452.56 = 17452.24.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.adjusted_annual_rate: 21409. Benefit income (Social Security, FERS annuity and compensation): statement 17452.24 received today (fresh) -> used as stated (standard: 24000.00 - 7440.00 = 16560.00). Spouse 7440.00, level 2023-12-01, 34 months -> x1.0537 = 7839.53. Countable income 25291.77. Threshold 5 percent of the category's basic rate 22838 = 1141.90. Medical deduction 25005.60 - 1141.90 = 23863.70, positive and smaller than 25291.77 -> income after deduction 1428.07 (standard income whole); 22838 - 1428.07 = 21409.93 -> 21409.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.gross_amount: 7566.47. New monthly floor(21409/12) = 1784. Months owed: 6 monthly payments issued since 2026-04-01 (standard through the current month, 7). Already paid: the monthly payments issued in those months (413 x3, 463 x3 = 2628.00) plus the earlier June release 50.00 = 2678.00. Returned June payment: 413.00 came back -> +413.00. Monthly compensation since 2025-12-01 subtracted: 721.68. Retroactive compensation: fee agreement, fee 133.11 within the cap -> 754.26 considered; pension-month share (2 - 1 lag) / 5 = 0.2 -> 150.85 subtracted. 1784 x 6 - 2678.00 + 413.00 - 721.68 - 150.85 = 7566.47.

edges.condition: pension_income_reports holds a pension_rate_adjusted entry on the award, recorded after the most recent monthly payment, whose adjusted_annual_rate divided by 12 and rounded down exceeds that payment's gross_amount and whose change_effective_date precedes it.
edges.policy_source: A retroactive release for months already paid is not issued until the award carries a rate adjustment that raises the annual pension for those months.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only rate adjustment on the award is the premium adjustment of 2026-07-14 (annual 5565 -> monthly 463), which equals the September payment of 463.00 and does not raise the rate; the care months reported on 2026-08-11 have never been applied.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 11 records an adjustment effective 2026-04-01 with annual 21409 (monthly 1784 > 463), so new_annual becomes 21409 and the release is 7566.47.

edges.policy_source: The new annual rate is fixed only after the award carries a benefit income statement from the veteran dated on the day his VA disability compensation stopped.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (statement -> adjustment -> release); no problem has two prerequisites, so there are no parallel edges to order. Each write is consumed by the next: the adjustment reads the statement's amount and the release reads the adjustment's annual pension and effective date.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without step 11 the latest adjustment is the 2026-07-14 one (5565 -> 463 a month, not above the 463.00 paid), so the release computes to 0 instead of 7566.47 and the retroactive payment row differs.
Without step 9 no statement exists, the benefit income falls back to the award's 16560.00 and the adjusted annual rate is 22302 instead of 21409; the statement row is also missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for the back pension owed for the care bills he mailed. It carries no statement of how VA handles care bills or back pay (the earlier neighbor remark was removed in rework round 2), never mentions an income statement, a rate adjustment or a recomputation; compensation, the bank change, the annuity, Arlene's income and aide details come up only if the representative asks, and he submits something personally only after the representative explains and hands it over.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: In task_tools.py, certify_benefit_income_d2f4edcf, record_rate_adjustment_fee79930 and release_retro_payment_a1af7a43 each perform one ctx.create with the arguments given and return a receipt; none reads the award's reports to test whether a statement or a raising adjustment exists, none refuses, and none returns an error when a prerequisite is unmet (for example release_retro_payment_a1af7a43 would write a release under the 2026-07-14 adjustment if called without step 11).
